Subject: Proposal: Onramp Velocity & Pricing Redlines

Alyssa — attaching the latest onramp pricing proposal and a MAP timeline that ties discounts to concrete checkpoints. Key points up front: 

- 6-week evaluation window (pilot) to validate throughput and latency at 10k monthly active tokens.
- Commit structure post-eval: month-to-month for first 3 months, then quarterly commitments with a ramp schedule to reach a 3x baseline by month 6.
- Pricing: base per-token rate $0.004; 15% aggregate discount if ClearWave hits the month-3 checkpoint (50% of target), 25% if month-6 checkpoint met.
- We propose a one-time onboarding credit of $30k tied to executing the MAP and final SOW within 30 days. Credit payable as pre-invoice credit on month 1.

Attached: redlined_term_sheet_v3.pdf (high level commercial terms), MAP_timeline_v2.xlsx (milestones + acceptance criteria).

Next steps: please review the redlines with your legal team and let us know which items you need us to adjust. If acceptable, we can push a DocuSign packet for signature and schedule a technical acceptance checkpoint at week 4.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this forward.

—
Grace O'Connor

From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@clearwave.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal - ClearWave <legal@clearwave.ai>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 10:02:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Proposal: Onramp Velocity & Pricing Redlines

Grace — thanks for this. We reviewed with product and legal; high level we're aligned on the MAP cadence but legal submitted a redline with a couple of sticking points: 

1) Definition of "ramp" — legal wants clearer metrics (we propose active inference tokens + 95th pct latency SLO) rather than just % of baseline.
2) Audit and data access — ClearWave needs explicit SOC2 evidence plus a narrower scope for support-side incident access (API keys limited to named SREs).
3) Discount clawback language — legal would like a 90-day lookback on discounts in case of prolonged underperformance (we'd prefer a one-off adjustment at check-in).
4) SLA credits — legal wants a minimum uptime SLA and monetary credits tied to breaches.

I've attached our redlined copy (redlined_term_sheet_v3.pdf) — their comments are inline.

Can you confirm if Redwood can: (a) formalize the ramp metric as tokens + latency; (b) accept a narrower access scope for audits; and (c) adjust the discount clause to a 60-day reconciliation instead of immediate clawback?

If we can get these reconciled, ClearWave is ready to sign the MAP and push the pilot into effect within two weeks.

Best,
Alyssa
Director, Product Partnerships
ClearWave AI

Attachment: redlined_term_sheet_v3.pdf (customer redlines)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 09:23:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Re: Proposal: Onramp Velocity & Pricing Redlines

Grace / Ben — forwarding Alyssa's legal notes. Summary and internal ask: 

- Ramp metric: agree to define as monthly active inference tokens (MAIT) + 95th percentile tail latency <= 250ms for the pilot (on hosted Redwood endpoints). If we need tighter latency in customer's region we can offer a higher SLA tier (Dedicated).
- Audit access: propose to accept SOC2 attestation + scoped support account access limited to two named SREs, with notifications and temporary tokens (90-day rotation). Security will need to sign off but this aligns with our Private plan controls.
- Discount reconciliation: recommend counter-offer to 60-day reconciliation with a one-time back-adjustment (no retroactive clawbacks beyond 60 days).
- SLA credits: offer service credits up to 5% of monthly invoice for major outages, escalate to enterprise team for anything beyond that.

Internal approvals needed: 
1) Concession on discount reconciliation (60 days) — MarComm approval? Finance OK with potential 5% credit exposure?
2) One-time onboarding credit of $30k — CS/Finance sign-off.

If folks are okay, I suggest we offer a "final" term sheet (v4) with those updates and include a DocuSign packet + a proposed technical acceptance date (week 4). I can draft the language for the ramp metric and discount reconciliation if you want.

—Marissa
Sr. Manager, Commercial Operations
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Subject: Final: Onramp velocity terms (v4) — signoff path and DocuSign

Alyssa — thanks for the patience; attached is term sheet v4 with our negotiated language. Highlights of what's changed based on your legal notes and our internal review: 

- Ramp metric: MAIT (monthly active inference tokens) + 95th pct latency <= 250ms measured on Redwood hosted endpoints for pilot. We added a clause for regional performance variance and an enterprise SLA upgrade option.
- Audit & access: we will provide SOC2 Type II report and scoped temporary support tokens limited to two named SREs; tokens rotate every 90 days; all access is logged and available to ClearWave upon request.
- Discount reconciliation: 60-day reconciliation window; one-time back-adjustment to the invoice following reconciliation; no retrospective clawbacks prior to signed MAP.
- Onboarding credit: $30k applied as a month-1 invoice credit once MAP and SOW are fully executed.
- SLA credits: capped at 5% of monthly invoice for qualifying downtime events; enterprise escalation path for anything beyond the cap.

I've also included a proposed MAP acceptance schedule in MAP_timeline_v2.xlsx and a DocuSign link to v4 (https://www.docusign.com/checkout/sign/CW-onramp-2026). If ClearWave confirms the two named SREs for tokened support access, we can issue the DocuSign and target tech acceptance week 4 from signature (pilot start = signature date + 7 days).

Questions for you: 
1) Accept the 60-day reconciliation for the discount?
2) Confirm two SREs for scoped support tokens (names + emails)?
3) If yes to both, we'll issue DocuSign today and schedule the tech check-in for week 4.

If you prefer, I can also schedule a 30-min call this week to walk legal through redlines.

Best regards,
